Plan in advance how you will restart when habits slip.

activity.title: Write your 90-day plan
steps: Score your Module 1 OKR from 0 to 1 for each key result.
Write a new OKR for the next 90 days.
Name your next time-drain target and the change you will test.
Enter your keeper habits as repeating Google Calendar events.
Write two if-then slip rules and check your evidence against the certification checklist.
activity.evidence: Your one-page 90-day plan, a screenshot of the repeating calendar events and the completed certification checklist.

quiz.q: Which hypothesis is best for a two-week experiment?
options: I will try to be more productive
If I block 9 to 11 a.m. for deep work, my focused hours will rise from 1 to 2 a day within two weeks
I will use all the methods from the course at once
If I work harder, things will improve
quiz.explain: A good hypothesis names one change, a measure, a baseline, a target and a time frame.

quiz.q: Rukayat's experiment included a week with a site inspection. How should she handle this in her comparison?
options: Leave that week out without mentioning it
Use only her best day as the result
Note the unusual factor next to her averaged results
quiz.explain: Honest comparisons use averages and note anything unusual that may have affected the numbers.

quiz.q: Which is the strongest CV line?
options: Cut daily interruptions from 23 to 7 by introducing scheduled message batches, doubling focused work time
quiz.explain: It names the change, the measure and the result with numbers, which makes it believable.

quiz.q: In the STAR interview structure, what does the A stand for?
options: Action: what you did, step by step
quiz.explain: STAR is Situation, Task, Action, Result. Action describes the steps you took.

quiz.q: Halima reached 30 repeat customers against a key result target of 40. What is her score on a 0 to 1 scale?
quiz.explain: 30 divided by 40 is 0.75.

quiz.q: Which is the best example of a slip rule in a 90-day plan?
options: I will never miss a weekly review
I will try harder next quarter
If I miss my weekly review twice in a row, I will do a 20-minute version next Monday morning
I will stop tracking if it gets difficult
quiz.explain: A slip rule is a specific if-then plan for getting back on track when a habit breaks.

finalQuiz.q: Amaka listed 14 tasks from her Tuesday and only 5 served a results area. What should she do first?
options: Work longer hours to finish all 14
Protect time each day for deep work on a key result
finalQuiz.explain: Lesson 1.1: output comes from protected time on key results, not from more activity.

finalQuiz.q: Which statement is a well-formed OKR key result?
options: Get 20 office catering orders by 30 September
Be the best caterer in Abuja
finalQuiz.explain: A key result is a measurable outcome with a date. "Be the best" is an objective-style statement and the others are activities.

finalQuiz.q: In her baseline, Funke recorded 69 interruptions over 3 days. What is her average per day?
finalQuiz.explain: 69 divided by 3 is 23 interruptions per day.

finalQuiz.q: Which item is written as a GTD next action?
options: Call Mr Okafor to confirm the delivery date
finalQuiz.explain: A next action starts with a verb and is a visible, physical step you could take now.

finalQuiz.q: Where should a board meeting fixed for Thursday at 10 a.m. go?
finalQuiz.explain: Only items tied to a specific day or time go in the calendar; actions without a fixed time go on task lists.

finalQuiz.q: What is the standard Pomodoro cycle?
options: 25 minutes focus, short break, and a longer break after four sessions
Work until tired, then stop for the day
finalQuiz.explain: Francesco Cirillo's technique uses 25-minute focus sessions with short breaks and a longer break after four.

finalQuiz.q: Which Gmail feature lets you write a reply at 10 p.m. but deliver it at 8 a.m.?
finalQuiz.explain: Schedule send delivers the email at a time you choose, so you do not set late-night expectations.

finalQuiz.q: Bukola wants busy groups to stop interrupting her but still wants to read them later. What should she use?
options: Mute the groups and check them in a set batch time
finalQuiz.explain: Muted chats still receive messages without interrupting her, and a batch time ensures she reads them.

finalQuiz.q: Which part of a delegation brief states "You can spend up to 20,000 naira without asking me"?
finalQuiz.explain: Authority defines what the person can decide alone and what needs approval.

finalQuiz.q: A colleague is regularly online until midnight, more cynical about work and making unusual mistakes. Which WHO burn-out dimensions do these signs match?
options: None, this is normal for busy people
Exhaustion, mental distance and reduced efficacy
finalQuiz.explain: Long hours with depletion, cynicism and falling effectiveness match all three WHO dimensions.

finalQuiz.q: Ngozi's scorecard shows priorities often unfinished but focused hours are good. What is the most likely cause?
options: She is planning more than her real capacity
Her weekly review is too short
finalQuiz.explain: If focus time is good but priorities stay unfinished, the plan is probably bigger than her capacity.

finalQuiz.q: Why should a productivity experiment test only one change at a time?
options: Because more changes are not allowed
Because two changes take too long to set up
Because results are only valid for one day
So that any improvement can be linked to that change
finalQuiz.explain: With one change, a difference from the baseline can be attributed to it; several changes at once hide which one worked.

capstone.title: Personal Productivity Improvement Project
capstone.brief: Measure your working baseline, test one specific change for at least two weeks, and submit an evidence pack: three-day baseline log, OKR, screenshots of your task and calendar system, at least two weekly scorecards, experiment hypothesis and before-and-after table, a one-page report and a 90-day plan.
steps: Log three working days and calculate focused hours, interruptions per day, percentage of time on results and planned capacity; name your biggest time drain.
Write a quarterly OKR (one objective, three key results) linked to your key results areas.
Set up your task system (Google Tasks lists and a Keep inbox), time-block at least three days and set up message controls.
Write a hypothesis for one change aimed at your biggest time drain and run it for at least two weeks, tracking the same measures as your baseline.
Run weekly reviews and record your scorecard each week.
Build a before-and-after table, decide keep, adjust or drop, and write a one-page report.
Score your OKR and write a 90-day plan with a new OKR, your next time-drain target, scheduled keeper habits and slip rules.
evidence: Three-day baseline log with the four baseline numbers and named time drain
Written OKR and its end-of-course score
Screenshots of Google Tasks lists, three time-blocked days and message controls
At least two completed weekly scorecards
Written hypothesis, daily tracking notes and before-and-after table with unusual factors noted
One-page report with problem, change, results, value and next step
90-day plan with repeating calendar events and two slip rules
